description: A dermatophyte infection of the body surface, commonly known as body ringworm.
causes: Dermatophyte fungi, predominantly Trichophyton and Microsporum species
risk_factors: Contact with infected people or pets

appearance.general: A superficial scaly eruption on the body; lesions may have an expanding edge as the infection spreads.

general_first_aid: Keep affected skin clean and dry.
prevention: Avoid sharing towels, clothing, and bedding with infected people.
Avoid close contact with infected individuals until appropriately managed.
Consider household members and pets as possible sources when recurrent infection occurs.
doctor_discussion_points: Discuss whether skin scraping or fungal testing is needed when the diagnosis is uncertain.
Mention other tinea sites or recurrent infections.
